- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- In periods with high sentiment volatility (alternating +/– > 1.0), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon; reduce first 5–7 days by 2–5% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to underestimate the rebound; add 1–2% buffer to forecast during recovery phase.
